# CodeBlock

A block of code in the code typeface on the code surface, with optional line numbers and highlighted lines. Long lines scroll sideways inside a focusable, named region, or fold onto the next line when `wrap` is on. It does not color syntax: the text is one ink, and `language` is recorded for tools.

**Import:** `import { CodeBlock } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.stories.jsx` — Overview, WithoutLineNumbers, HighlightedLines, SeparateHighlights, ScrollsLongLines, WrapsLongLines, BlankLines, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, WrapNotFocusable

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.mdx`

## Usage

Use `CodeBlock` for code a reader may copy or follow line by line: an example,
a command sequence, a config file. For a name or short phrase inside a
sentence, use `Code`.

The typeface is the `--code` text style at 0.875rem on a 1.25rem line. The
surface is `--ds-background-code-default`, the ink `--ds-text-code-default`, the
gutter `--ds-background-code-gutter` with `--ds-text-code-gutter`, and a
highlighted line `--ds-background-code-highlight`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Show the smallest snippet that makes the point. | Paste a whole file. |
| Name the language in prose before the block. | Leave the reader to guess the language or the file name. |
| Highlight the lines the text is about. | Highlight most of the block. |
| Give each block a `label` when a page has several. | Leave several blocks with the same name. |

## Best practices

### Scroll commands, wrap prose. {#scroll-commands-wrap-prose}

Scroll keeps line structure, which matters for shell commands and config, where a fold could read as a new line. Wrap suits prose-like output in a narrow column.

Do: A command scrolls, so one line stays one line.
Don't: A command folded onto a second line reads like two commands.

### Name each block when there are several on a page. {#name-each-block-when-there-are-several-on-a-page}

Do: Each region says what it holds: Install command.
Don't: Every block named Code snippet.

### Do not rely on a highlight alone. {#do-not-rely-on-a-highlight-alone}

Do: The sentence says which line to read, and the highlight supports it.
Don't: The fill is the only cue.

### Keep the numbers for code you discuss. {#keep-the-numbers-for-code-you-discuss}

Do: A one-line command with no gutter.
Don't: A line number beside a single command.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard scroll.** A scrolling block is a focusable region with a name, so a
  keyboard user can scroll it with the arrow keys. A wrapping block has nothing
  to scroll and is not a tab stop.
- **Highlights are spoken.** Each highlighted run is bracketed by "Highlight
  start" and "Highlight end" for screen readers, because fill alone says nothing
  to them. Those words are not selectable, so they stay out of a copy.
- **Line numbers are skipped.** The gutter is hidden from assistive technology and
  cannot be selected, so a copy is the code alone.
- **Contrast.** Ink, gutter and highlight come from the code color roles and keep
  their contrast in every color and contrast mode.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | `''` | The code, with lines separated by newlines. |
| `language` | string | — | The language, recorded as a `language- ` class for tools that read it. It does not color the text. |
| `showLineNumbers` | bool | `true` | Whether each line is numbered in a gutter that screen readers skip. |
| `highlight` | string or number or arrayOf | — | Lines to highlight: a string such as "2,4-6", or an array such as [1, 3]. Start and end are announced to screen readers. |
| `wrap` | bool | `false` | Fold long lines onto the next line instead of scrolling sideways. |
| `label` | string | `'Code snippet'` | The name of the scrolling region a screen reader announces. Unused when `wrap` is on. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra classes for placement, such as spacing. |
